sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śreyo vai yācataḥ pārtha dattam āhur ayācate arhattamo vai dhṛtimān kṛpaṇād adhṛtātmanaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: A gift bestowed upon one who does not beg is held more meritorious than one given to a beggar, O Pārtha; for the steadfast man is far worthier of honor than the wretch whose soul lacks self-command.

sanskrit: kṣatriyo rakṣaṇadhṛtir brāhmaṇo 'narthanādhṛtiḥ brāhmaṇo dhṛtimān vidvān devān prīṇāti tuṣṭimān
english: The kṣatriya is steadfast in protection, the brāhmaṇa steadfast in not soliciting; the learned and contented brāhmaṇa, firm of resolve, gives delight to the gods.

sanskrit: yācñām āhur anīśasya abhihāraṃ ca bhārata udvejayati yācan hi sadā bhūtāni dasyuvat
english: Begging, O Bhārata, they call the resort of the powerless, a kind of seizing; for he who begs ever distresses living beings, like a robber.

sanskrit: mriyate yācamāno vai tam anu mriyate dadat dadat saṃjīvayaty enam ātmānaṃ ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: The one who begs is as good as dead, and the giver dies along with him if he refuses; but by giving, O Yudhiṣṭhira, he keeps that suppliant alive, and himself as well.

sanskrit: ānṛśaṃsyaṃ paro dharmo yācate yat pradīyate ayācataḥ sīdamānān sarvopāyair nimantraya
english: Freedom from cruelty is the supreme dharma, which is fulfilled in what is given to one who begs; but those who suffer in silence and do not ask, invite them by every means.

sanskrit: yadi vai tādṛśā rāṣṭre vaseyus te dvijottamāḥ bhasmacchannān ivāgnīṃs tān budhyethās tvaṃ prayatnataḥ
english: If such foremost of the twice-born should dwell within your realm, take pains to recognize them, like fires hidden beneath their ashes.

sanskrit: tapasā dīpyamānās te daheyuḥ pṛthivīm api pūjyā hi jñānavijñānatapoyogasamanvitāḥ
english: Blazing with their austerity, they could consume even the earth; for they are worthy of worship, endowed with knowledge, discernment, austerity, and yoga.

sanskrit: tebhyaḥ pūjāṃ prayuñjīthā brāhmaṇebhyaḥ paraṃtapa dadad bahuvidhān dāyān upacchandān ayācatām
english: Offer worship to those brāhmaṇas, O scorcher of foes, bestowing gifts of many kinds, and coaxing forth those who do not ask.

sanskrit: yad agnihotre suhute sāyaṃprātar bhavet phalam vidyāvedavratavati tad dānaphalam ucyate
english: Whatever fruit accrues from the agnihotra well-offered at evening and at dawn, that same fruit is declared to belong to a gift made to one possessed of learning, Veda, and vows.

sanskrit: vidyāvedavratasnātān avyapāśrayajīvinaḥ gūḍhasvādhyāyatapaso brāhmaṇān saṃśitavratān
english: Those brāhmaṇas who have bathed in the close of learning, Veda, and vows, who live without dependence on others, whose private study and austerity are hidden, who are firm in their vows—

sanskrit: kṛtair āvasathair hṛdyaiḥ sapreṣyaiḥ saparicchadaiḥ nimantrayethāḥ kaunteya kāmaiś cānyair dvijottamān
english: with pleasing dwellings built for them, furnished with servants and appointments, you should invite those foremost of the twice-born, O son of Kuntī, and with other things they desire.

sanskrit: api te pratigṛhṇīyuḥ śraddhāpūtaṃ yudhiṣṭhira kāryam ity eva manvānā dharmajñāḥ sūkṣmadarśinaḥ
english: Perhaps they will accept what is hallowed by faith, O Yudhiṣṭhira, thinking only that it must be done—knowers of dharma, seers of the subtle.

sanskrit: api te brāhmaṇā bhuktvā gatāḥ soddharaṇān gṛhān yeṣāṃ dārāḥ pratīkṣante parjanyam iva karṣakāḥ
english: Perhaps those brāhmaṇas, having eaten, will return to homes with stores laid by, whose wives await them as farmers await the rain-cloud.

sanskrit: annāni prātaḥsavane niyatā brahmacāriṇaḥ brāhmaṇās tāta bhuñjānās tretāgnīn prīṇayantu te
english: Let the brāhmaṇas, disciplined celibates, partaking of food at the morning pressing, my child, give delight thereby to your three sacred fires.

sanskrit: mādhyaṃdinaṃ te savanaṃ dadatas tāta vartatām gā hiraṇyāni vāsāṃsi tenendraḥ prīyatāṃ tava
english: Let your midday pressing proceed, my child, as you give cattle, gold, and garments; by that may Indra be pleased with you.

sanskrit: tṛtīyaṃ savanaṃ tat te vaiśvadevaṃ yudhiṣṭhira yad devebhyaḥ pitṛbhyaś ca viprebhyaś ca prayacchasi
english: That is your third, the Vaiśvadeva pressing, O Yudhiṣṭhira, in what you bestow upon the gods, the ancestors, and the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā sarvabhūtebhyaḥ saṃvibhāgaś ca sarvaśaḥ damas tyāgo dhṛtiḥ satyaṃ bhavatv avabhṛthāya te
english: Non-injury toward all beings, sharing in every way, self-restraint, renunciation, steadfastness, and truth—let these serve as your concluding bath of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: eṣa te vitato yajñaḥ śraddhāpūtaḥ sadakṣiṇaḥ viśiṣṭaḥ sarvayajñebhyo nityaṃ tāta pravartatām
english: This is your sacrifice spread wide, hallowed by faith, attended with its offerings, surpassing all sacrifices; may it ever go forward, my child.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dānaṃ yajñakriyā ceha kiṃ svit pretya mahāphalam kasya jyāyaḥ phalaṃ proktaṃ kīdṛśebhyaḥ kathaṃ kadā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Of giving and the rite of sacrifice here, which yields the greater fruit hereafter? Whose fruit is declared the loftier—and to what kind of recipients, how, and when?

sanskrit: etad icchāmi vijñātuṃ yāthātathyena bhārata vidvañ jijñāsamānāya dānadharmān pracakṣva me
english: This I wish to know truly as it is, O Bhārata; learned one, to me who seeks to understand, expound the laws of giving.

sanskrit: antarvedyāṃ ca yad dattaṃ śraddhayā cānṛśaṃsyataḥ kiṃ svin niḥśreyasaṃ tāta tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: What is given within the altar-ground, with faith and without cruelty—which of these brings the highest good, my father? Tell me that, grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca raudraṃ karma kṣatriyasya satataṃ tāta vartate tasya vaitānikaṃ karma dānaṃ caiveha pāvanam
english: Bhīṣma said: The work of the kṣatriya is forever fierce, my child; for him the rite of the sacred fires and giving are the purifiers in this world.

sanskrit: na tu pāpakṛtāṃ rājñāṃ pratigṛhṇanti sādhavaḥ etasmāt kāraṇād yajñair yajed rājāptadakṣiṇaiḥ
english: But the good do not accept gifts from kings who do evil; for this reason a king should worship with sacrifices furnished with well-earned offerings.

sanskrit: atha cet pratigṛhṇīyur dadyād aharahar nṛpaḥ śraddhām āsthāya paramāṃ pāvanaṃ hy etad uttamam
english: But if they do accept, let the king give day after day, taking his stand on the highest faith; for this is the supreme purification.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāṃs tarpayed dravyais tato yajñe yatavrataḥ maitrān sādhūn vedavidaḥ śīlavṛttataponvitān
english: Let him, his vows controlled, satisfy with gifts the brāhmaṇas at the sacrifice—the friendly, the good, the knowers of the Veda, endowed with character, conduct, and austerity.

sanskrit: yat te tena kariṣyanti kṛtaṃ tena bhaviṣyati yajñān sādhaya sādhubhyaḥ svādvannān dakṣiṇāvataḥ
english: Whatever they shall accomplish thereby will become an accomplished deed for you; bring sacrifices to fulfillment for the good, with savory food and ample offerings.

sanskrit: iṣṭaṃ dattaṃ ca manyethā ātmānaṃ dānakarmaṇā pūjayethā yāyajūkāṃs tavāpy aṃśo bhaved yathā
english: Deem yourself to have sacrificed and given; by the act of giving honor those constant in sacrifice, that a share thereof may be yours as well.

sanskrit: prajāvato bharethāś ca brāhmaṇān bahubhāriṇaḥ prajāvāṃs tena bhavati yathā janayitā tathā
english: Support too the brāhmaṇas blessed with offspring and burdened with many to feed; by this one becomes rich in progeny, even as the begetter himself.

sanskrit: yāvato vai sādhudharmān santaḥ saṃvartayanty uta sarve te cāpi bhartavyā narā ye bahubhāriṇaḥ
english: As many righteous observances as the good keep alive, so many of those men who bear heavy burdens of dependents must likewise be maintained.

sanskrit: samṛddhaḥ saṃprayacchasva brāhmaṇebhyo yudhiṣṭhira dhenūr anaḍuho 'nnāni cchatraṃ vāsāṃsy upānahau
english: Prosperous as you are, bestow upon the brāhmaṇas, O Yudhiṣṭhira, milch-cows, oxen, food, a parasol, garments, and sandals.

sanskrit: ājyāni yajamānebhyas tathānnādyāni bhārata aśvavanti ca yānāni veśmāni śayanāni ca
english: Clarified butter to the sacrificers, and food and viands, O Bhārata, and conveyances drawn by horses, dwellings, and beds.

sanskrit: ete deyā vyuṣṭimanto laghūpāyāś ca bhārata ajugupsāṃś ca vijñāya brāhmaṇān vṛttikarśitān
english: These are to be given—fruitful and easily come by, O Bhārata—once you have marked out the blameless brāhmaṇas worn thin by want of livelihood.

sanskrit: upacchannaṃ prakāśaṃ vā vṛttyā tān pratipādaya rājasūyāśvamedhābhyāṃ śreyas tat kṣatriyān prati
english: Whether in secret or in the open, provide them with a livelihood; for a kṣatriya that is more excellent than the Rājasūya and the Aśvamedha.

sanskrit: evaṃ pāpair vimuktas tvaṃ pūtaḥ svargam avāpsyasi sraṃsayitvā punaḥ kośaṃ yad rāṣṭraṃ pālayiṣyasi
english: Thus freed from your sins and made pure, you shall attain heaven, when, having loosed your treasury again, you shall protect your realm.

sanskrit: tataś ca brahmabhūyastvam avāpsyasi dhanāni ca ātmanaś ca pareṣāṃ ca vṛttiṃ saṃrakṣa bhārata
english: And thereafter you shall attain oneness with Brahman, and wealth besides; guard well the livelihood of yourself and of others, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: putravac cāpi bhṛtyān svān prajāś ca paripālaya yogakṣemaś ca te nityaṃ brāhmaṇeṣv astu bhārata
english: Cherish your servants and your subjects as you would your sons; and let your care for their welfare and security ever rest upon the brāhmaṇas, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: arakṣitāraṃ hartāraṃ viloptāram adāyakam taṃ sma rājakaliṃ hanyuḥ prajāḥ saṃbhūya nirghṛṇam
english: A king who does not protect but seizes, who plunders and gives nothing—that disgrace among kings, that pitiless one, the people, banding together, would do well to slay.

sanskrit: ahaṃ vo rakṣitety uktvā yo na rakṣati bhūmipaḥ sa saṃhatya nihantavyaḥ śveva sonmāda āturaḥ
english: The lord of earth who says 'I am your protector' yet does not protect—him should the people unite to kill, like a mad and rabid dog.

sanskrit: pāpaṃ kurvanti yat kiṃ cit prajā rājñā hy arakṣitāḥ caturthaṃ tasya pāpasya rājā bhārata vindati
english: Whatever evil the subjects commit when left unprotected by the king, a fourth part of that evil the king incurs, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: apy āhuḥ sarvam eveti bhūyo 'rdham iti niścayaḥ caturthaṃ matam asmākaṃ manoḥ śrutvānuśāsanam
english: Some say it is the whole; others fix it firmly at a half; but a fourth is our own view, having heard the teaching of Manu.

sanskrit: śubhaṃ vā yat prakurvanti prajā rājñā surakṣitāḥ caturthaṃ tasya puṇyasya rājā cāpnoti bhārata
english: And whatever good the subjects do when well protected by the king, a fourth part of that merit the king obtains, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: jīvantaṃ tvānujīvantu prajāḥ sarvā yudhiṣṭhira parjanyam iva bhūtāni mahādrumam iva dvijāḥ
english: May all your subjects live in dependence on your life, O Yudhiṣṭhira, as living beings on the rain-cloud, as birds upon a mighty tree.

sanskrit: kuberam iva rakṣāṃsi śatakratum ivāmarāḥ jñātayas tvānujīvantu suhṛdaś ca paraṃtapa
english: As the rākṣasas live in dependence on Kubera, as the immortals on Indra of the hundred sacrifices, so may your kinsmen and friends live in dependence on you, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca idaṃ deyam idaṃ deyam itīyaṃ śruticodanā bahudeyāś ca rājānaḥ kiṃ svid deyam anuttamam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: 'This is to be given, this is to be given'—so runs the injunction of scripture, and kings have many things to give; but what gift is the most excellent of all?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ati dānāni sarvāṇi pṛthivīdānam ucyate acalā hy akṣayā bhūmir dogdhrī kāmān anuttamān
english: Bhīṣma said: Surpassing all gifts, the gift of land is proclaimed supreme; for the earth is unmoving and imperishable, yielding desires that have no equal.

sanskrit: dogdhrī vāsāṃsi ratnāni paśūn vrīhiyavāṃs tathā bhūmidaḥ sarvabhūteṣu śāśvatīr edhate samāḥ
english: She yields garments, gems, cattle, rice, and barley; the giver of land flourishes among all beings for everlasting years.

sanskrit: yāvad bhūmer āyur iha tāvad bhūmida edhate na bhūmidānād astīha paraṃ kiṃ cid yudhiṣṭhira
english: As long as the life of the earth endures, so long does the giver of land flourish; there is nothing here higher than the gift of land, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: apy alpaṃ pradaduḥ pūrve pṛthivyā iti naḥ śrutam bhūmim ete daduḥ sarve ye bhūmiṃ bhuñjate janāḥ
english: Even a little of the earth the ancients gave, so we have heard; all those people who enjoy the use of land have in truth given land.

sanskrit: svakarmaivopajīvanti narā iha paratra ca bhūmir bhūtir mahādevī dātāraṃ kurute priyam
english: By their own deeds alone do men live, here and hereafter; the earth, prosperity itself, the great goddess, makes the giver dear to her.

sanskrit: ya etāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dadyād akṣayāṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ punar naratvaṃ saṃprāpya bhavet sa pṛthivīpatiḥ
english: That lord of earth who bestows this imperishable gift, on attaining human birth once more, shall himself become a lord of earth.

sanskrit: yathā dānaṃ tathā bhoga iti dharmeṣu niścayaḥ saṃgrāme vā tanuṃ jahyād dadyād vā pṛthivīm imām
english: As the gift, so the enjoyment—such is the settled rule in the codes of dharma; let a man either yield up his body in battle or give away this earth.

sanskrit: ity etāṃ kṣatrabandhūnāṃ vadanti param āśiṣam punāti dattā pṛthivī dātāram iti śuśruma
english: This they declare to be the highest blessing of the warrior kinsmen; the earth, once given, purifies the giver—so have we heard.

sanskrit: api pāpasamācāraṃ brahmaghnam api vānṛtam saiva pāpaṃ pāvayati saiva pāpāt pramocayet
english: Even him whose conduct is sinful, even a slayer of a brāhmaṇa or a speaker of falsehood—she alone cleanses of that sin, she alone can release from sin.

sanskrit: api pāpakṛtāṃ rājñāṃ pratigṛhṇanti sādhavaḥ pṛthivīṃ nānyad icchanti pāvanaṃ jananī yathā
english: Even from kings who do evil the good accept the earth, and desire nothing else; for she purifies like a mother.

sanskrit: nāmāsyāḥ priyadatteti guhyaṃ devyāḥ sanātanam dānaṃ vāpy atha vā jñānaṃ nāmno 'syāḥ paramaṃ priyam tasmāt prāpyaiva pṛthivīṃ dadyād viprāya pārthivaḥ
english: 'Priyadattā'—'Dear when given'—is the secret, eternal name of this goddess; either gift or knowledge is dearest to that name of hers. Therefore, no sooner has a king won the earth than he should give it to a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: nābhūmipatinā bhūmir adhiṣṭheyā kathaṃ cana na vā pātreṇa vā gūhed antardhānena vā caret ye cānye bhūmim iccheyuḥ kuryur evam asaṃśayam
english: By no means may the earth be held by one who is not a lord of the soil; nor should one conceal it through a worthy proxy, nor proceed by stealth. And whoever else might covet land should act in this same way, beyond all doubt.

sanskrit: yaḥ sādhor bhūmim ādatte na bhūmiṃ vindate tu saḥ bhūmiṃ tu dattvā sādhubhyo vindate bhūmim eva hi pretyeha ca sa dharmātmā saṃprāpnoti mahad yaśaḥ
english: He who takes away a good man's land—he wins no land at all; but he who gives land to the good wins land indeed, and that righteous soul gains great renown both here and hereafter.

sanskrit: yasya viprānuśāsanti sādhor bhūmiṃ sadaiva hi na tasya śatravo rājan praśāsanti vasuṃdharām
english: He whose land the brāhmaṇas, being good, ever govern—his enemies, O king, never come to rule the earth.

sanskrit: yat kiṃ cit puruṣaḥ pāpaṃ kurute vṛttikarśitaḥ api gocarmamātreṇa bhūmidānena pūyate
english: Whatever sin a man commits, worn thin by want of livelihood, he is cleansed of it by the gift of land—even of land no larger than a cowhide.

sanskrit: ye 'pi saṃkīrṇakarmāṇo rājāno raudrakarmiṇaḥ tebhyaḥ pavitram ākhyeyaṃ bhūmidānam anuttamam
english: Even for those kings whose deeds are mixed and whose works are cruel, the supreme gift of land is to be proclaimed a means of purity.

sanskrit: alpāntaram idaṃ śaśvat purāṇā menire janāḥ yo yajed aśvamedhena dadyād vā sādhave mahīm
english: That the difference is ever but slight, the men of old held: between one who sacrifices with the Aśvamedha and one who gives the earth to a good man.

sanskrit: api cet sukṛtaṃ kṛtvā śaṅkerann api paṇḍitāḥ aśakyam ekam evaitad bhūmidānam anuttamam
english: Even when they have done a good deed, the wise may yet harbor misgiving; this one thing alone is beyond such doubt—the supreme, irreproachable gift of land.

sanskrit: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ vastraṃ maṇimuktāvasūni ca sarvam etan mahāprājña dadāti vasudhāṃ dadat
english: Gold, silver, garments, jewels, pearls, and riches—all this, O greatly wise one, the giver of the earth bestows in giving it.

sanskrit: tapo yajñaḥ śrutaṃ śīlam alobhaḥ satyasaṃdhatā gurudaivatapūjā ca nātivartanti bhūmidam
english: Austerity, sacrifice, sacred learning, character, freedom from greed, truthfulness, and worship of teachers and gods—none of these surpasses the giver of land.

sanskrit: bhartur niḥśreyase yuktās tyaktātmāno raṇe hatāḥ brahmalokagatāḥ siddhā nātikrāmanti bhūmidam
english: Those who, devoted to their lord's highest good, give up their lives and are slain in battle, the perfected who have gone to the world of Brahman—even they do not outstrip the giver of land.

sanskrit: yathā janitrī kṣīreṇa svaputraṃ bharate sadā anugṛhṇāti dātāraṃ tathā sarvarasair mahī
english: As a mother ever nourishes her own son with her milk, so does the earth favor the giver with all her savors.

sanskrit: mṛtyor vai kiṃkaro daṇḍas tāpo vahneḥ sudāruṇaḥ ghorāś ca vāruṇāḥ pāśā nopasarpanti bhūmidam
english: The rod that is Death's servant, the most dreadful burning of fire, and the terrible nooses of Varuṇa—none of these draws near the giver of land.

sanskrit: pitṝṃś ca pitṛlokasthān devaloke ca devatāḥ saṃtarpayati śāntātmā yo dadāti vasuṃdharām
english: The ancestors abiding in the world of the fathers and the gods in the world of the gods—both does that serene soul satisfy who gives away the earth.

sanskrit: kṛśāya mriyamāṇāya vṛttimlānāya sīdate bhūmiṃ vṛttikarīṃ dattvā satrī bhavati mānavaḥ
english: To the gaunt, the dying, the man wasted in his livelihood and sinking down, a man who gives sustaining land becomes as one who has performed a sacrificial session.

sanskrit: yathā dhāvati gaur vatsaṃ kṣīram abhyutsṛjanty uta evam eva mahābhāga bhūmir bhavati bhūmidam
english: As a cow runs to her calf, letting her milk flow freely, so, O highly blessed one, does the earth come to the giver of land.

sanskrit: halakṛṣṭāṃ mahīṃ dattvā sabījāṃ saphalām api udīrṇaṃ vāpi śaraṇaṃ tathā bhavati kāmadaḥ
english: By giving land plowed and sown, bearing seed and yielding fruit, or by giving a noble refuge, a man becomes a granter of desires.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaṃ vṛttasaṃpannam āhitāgniṃ śucivratam naraḥ pratigrāhya mahīṃ na yāti yamasādanam
english: The man who makes a brāhmaṇa accept land—one perfect in conduct, who has set up his sacred fires, pure in his vows—does not go to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: yathā candramaso vṛddhir ahany ahani jāyate tathā bhūmikṛtaṃ dānaṃ sasye sasye vivardhate
english: As the waxing of the moon comes day by day, so does the gift made of land increase with every crop.

sanskrit: atra gāthā bhūmigītāḥ kīrtayanti purāvidaḥ yāḥ śrutvā jāmadagnyena dattā bhūḥ kāśyapāya vai
english: On this the knowers of old recite the songs sung by the Earth herself, on hearing which the son of Jamadagni gave the earth to Kaśyapa.

sanskrit: mām evādatta māṃ datta māṃ dattvā mām avāpsyatha asmiṃl loke pare caiva tataś cājanane punaḥ
english: 'Receive me, give me; having given me, you shall win me again—in this world and in the next, and thereafter once more in birthlessness.'

sanskrit: ya imāṃ vyāhṛtiṃ veda brāhmaṇo brahmasaṃśritaḥ śrāddhasya hūyamānasya brahmabhūyaṃ sa gacchati
english: The brāhmaṇa, devoted to Brahman, who knows this utterance, at a śrāddha whose oblations are being offered attains oneness with Brahman.

sanskrit: kṛtyānām abhiśastānāṃ duriṣṭaśamanaṃ mahat prāyaścittam ahaṃ kṛtvā punāty ubhayato daśa
english: 'A mighty quelling am I of malign rites and curses, the calmer of ill-offered sacrifices; once a man has performed the expiation that I am, it purifies ten on either side.'

sanskrit: punāti ya idaṃ veda veda cāhaṃ tathaiva ca prakṛtiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ bhūmir vai śāśvatī matā
english: 'Whoever knows this is purified, and I myself am likewise the Veda; the source of all beings, the everlasting earth—so am I held.'

sanskrit: abhiṣicyaiva nṛpatiṃ śrāvayed imam āgamam yathā śrutvā mahīṃ dadyān nādadyāt sādhutaś ca tām
english: As soon as a king is consecrated, let this sacred lore be recited to him, that on hearing it he may give the earth and not take it from the good.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ kṛtsno brāhmaṇārtho rājārthaś cāpy asaṃśayam rājā hi dharmakuśalaḥ prathamaṃ bhūtilakṣaṇam
english: This, then, is the whole matter, both of the brāhmaṇa and of the king, beyond all doubt; for a king skilled in dharma is the foremost mark of prosperity.
